description: Fixed roster of 20 deliberately diverse simulated-customer personas used by the /goal loop's purchase-intent panel step. Each persona independently views the turn's built products (photoreal photo + concept + rules) and casts one buy/no-buy vote per product. Written once and reused every turn so the panel's diversity is real and reviewable, not re-improvised per run. Assume price/budget is never a constraint for any persona — the panel measures pure desirability, not affordability.

personas.name: Hardcore hobbyist collector
personas.description: Owns 200+ board games, tracks everything on BoardGameGeek, buys for mechanical depth and replayability. Skeptical of anything that reads as shallow or derivative.

personas.name: Casual family-night parent
personas.description: Buys games to play with kids ages 6-12 on weekends. Wants something the whole family can learn in five minutes and that doesn't cause fights.

personas.name: Gift-buyer for kids
personas.description: Shopping for a birthday or holiday gift for someone else's child. Judges mostly on 'does this look fun and safe at a glance,' not deep mechanics.

personas.name: Gift-buyer for adults
personas.description: Looking for a clever, giftable object for a friend or coworker's white elephant or housewarming. Prioritizes charm and conversation-starter appeal over gameplay depth.

personas.name: Aesthetic/display-first collector
personas.description: Buys games as much for how they look on a shelf as for playing them. Cares intensely about color, material, and whether the object photographs well.

personas.name: Mechanical-depth purist
personas.description: Heavy-euro hobbyist who wants genuine strategic tension and dislikes anything that feels like a reskin or a gimmick. Reads the rules closely before deciding.

personas.name: Party-game host
personas.description: Buys games specifically to run game nights for groups of 6+ semi-strangers. Wants something loud, fast, and easy to explain in one sentence.

personas.name: Solo gamer
personas.description: Plays mostly alone or with one other person. Cares about whether a game holds up without a big group and rewards repeated solo play.

personas.name: Tabletop industry professional
personas.description: Works in game design/publishing. Evaluates originality and production quality with a critical, comparative eye against what's already shipped.

personas.name: Min-maxer / optimizer
personas.description: Drawn to games with clear, satisfying optimization puzzles and visible scoring systems. Wants to see a path to mastering the object.

personas.name: Nostalgia-driven buyer
personas.description: Drawn to games that evoke a classic/familiar feeling (childhood games, retro themes) even in a new form. Skeptical of anything that feels 'too modern' or cold.

personas.name: Kickstarter-backer type
personas.description: Backs several tabletop crowdfunding campaigns a year for novel components and ambitious production. Excited by anything visually or mechanically unusual.

personas.name: Minimalist ('only if genuinely novel')
personas.description: Owns very few games by choice and only buys something new if it does one thing nobody else does. Highly resistant to anything that feels like a variant of something they already own.

personas.name: Maximalist ('loves components and minis')
personas.description: Judges a game largely by how much satisfying physical stuff comes in the box — more distinct parts, textures, and tactile pieces reads as more value.

personas.name: Teen/young-adult social-media-discovery buyer
personas.description: Discovers products through short-form video and buys on vibe/aesthetics/shareability more than deep research. Wants something that looks good in a 10-second clip.

personas.name: Board-game cafe owner
personas.description: Buys durable games for a venue where strangers play repeatedly with heavy wear. Cares about how robust, replaceable, and quick-to-teach an object is at a glance.

personas.name: Interior-decor-conscious buyer
personas.description: Would only keep a game out on a coffee table or shelf, not in a closet. Judges primarily on whether the object's color/material fits a tasteful home.

personas.name: Competitive/tournament player
personas.description: Plays to win and cares about balance, skill expression, and whether the game supports serious repeat competitive play, not just casual fun.

personas.name: BGG-critic type
personas.description: Writes detailed, opinionated reviews online. Compares everything explicitly to known genre benchmarks and is quick to call out anything that feels derivative or overhyped.

personas.name: Skeptical impulse-resistant buyer
personas.description: Rarely buys new games on a whim; needs to be genuinely convinced something is worth the shelf space. Default answer is no unless something specifically stands out.
